title: Questions this manual cannot answer, and one place it contradicts itself
note: These are first-class retrievable facts, not prompt instructions. Grounding refusal in data is what makes it reliable: the agent declines because a tool told it the answer does not exist, not because a system prompt asked it to be careful.

gaps.claim: The thickness x wire-diameter x gas x voltage x wire-feed-speed matrix is NOT in this manual. It is a decal on the inside of the welder door. The tungsten sizing chart is a separate decal on top of the welder.

absence.note: Wire feed speed values would be printed in in/min. The string never appears across all 48 pages.

pointers.quote: Refer to the Settings Chart on the inside of the Welder door.
Set Flow Gauge to SCFH value indicated on Settings Chart.
Consult Settings Chart, on top of Welder, to determine proper Tungsten Electrode size to be used with thickness of material to be welded.
Set Flow Gauge to SCFH value indicated on the Settings Chart on the inside of the Welder door.
Ensure gas flow rate is set according to Settings Chart.

gaps.correctBehavior: Refuse to state a voltage or wire-feed-speed number. Render the matrix with its real axes and every cell hatched as not-in-manual, and direct the user to the door decal or the welder's own synergic screen, which computes these from process + wire diameter + material thickness + gas.
gaps.neverDo: Do not infer settings from general welding knowledge. Do not interpolate from the synergic examples. We cannot cite a decal we do not have.

gaps.claim: The machine's output range exceeds its published duty-cycle points in MIG on both input voltages. 240 V MIG reaches 220 A but nothing is published above 200 A; 120 V MIG reaches 140 A but nothing is published above 100 A.
gaps.correctBehavior: State the highest published point and that nothing is published above it. Render the duty-cycle matrix with the out-of-range column present and hatched, so the hole in the data is visible rather than described.
gaps.neverDo: Never extrapolate or interpolate a duty cycle. It is a tested thermal result under IEC 60974-1, not a function of amperage.

contradictions.quote: AC TIG Welding is used to weld aluminum using a TIG Rod and shielding gas.

refutedBy.reason: Output is DC only. The machine has no AC output, so it cannot perform AC TIG.

refutedBy.quote: Weldable Materials Mild Steel, Stainless Steel, Chrome Moly
refutedBy.reason: The TIG specification does not list aluminum as a weldable material.

contradictions.resolution: The p.28 line is generic boilerplate about the AC TIG process in general; it does not describe a capability of this machine. Aluminum on the OmniPro 220 is welded with the optional spool gun using MIG, not TIG.
contradictions.correctBehavior: Do not affirm that this machine can AC TIG aluminum. Surface the contradiction explicitly, cite both pages, and point the user to the spool gun path.
